stem.text: A particle moves in the \( xy \)-plane so that for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \) its velocity components are \( x'(t) = \sin(t^{2}) + 1 \) and \( y'(t) = e^{-t/2}\cos t \). At time \( t = 0 \) the particle is at the point \( (3, -1) \).

parts.prompt: Find the \( x \)-coordinate of the particle's position at time \( t = 2 \), and find the speed of the particle at time \( t = 2 \). Label each value you report.

worked_solution.text: Accumulate the x-velocity from the initial position.
Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector.

points.criterion: Writes x(2) as 3 plus the definite integral from 0 to 2 of sin(t^2) + 1 and reports 5.805 (or 5.804).
Writes the speed at t = 2 as the square root of x'(2)^2 + y'(2)^2 with the setup visible and reports 0.287.

Presents each of the two reported values with a label that identifies which quantity it is, such as x(2) = and speed =. Correctness of the values is judged by a1 and a2, so a value consistent with the student's own work counts here. Unlabelled values do not earn it.
